scope: French professional champions (Division 1 / Ligue 1) from 1932-33. Amateur-era championships (1893-1929, USFSA and others) are not included, so title counts here start at 1932-33 (e.g. Marseille 9, not the 10 the Wikipedia list shows including the 1929 amateur title). Wartime seasons 1939-40 to 1944-45 are not_held with the unofficial competitions described in notes. 1992-93 has no champion (Marseille stripped, see strippedChampion)
source: https://www.rsssf.org/tablesf/franchamp.html (RSSSF champions with W-D-L and points, every season; wartime competitions)
https://www.rsssf.org/tablesf/franYY.html / franYYYY.html (RSSSF final tables 1997-98 to 2025-26: top three and points)
Wikipedia season articles (YYYY–YY French Division 1 / Ligue 1) league tables and results grids (cross-check, points)

fieldNotes.footsimuId: ESPN team id (the id FootSimu uses); present for some clubs not in FootSimu leagues
fieldNotes.footsimuSlug: club page slug on footsimu.com, only for clubs in a FootSimu league in 2026-27
fieldNotes.footsimuPath: club page path under the league the club plays in now, without locale
fieldNotes.points: final points (2 per win until 1993-94, 3 from 1994-95; 1973-76 include bonus points); null for 1932-33 (two groups + final)
fieldNotes.name: club name used in the source for that season
fieldNotes.currentName: club as known today (FootSimu name where available); historic/defunct clubs are annotated
fieldNotes.strippedChampion: 1992-93 Marseille (title withdrawn, not awarded); champion is null in that season

notes: Inaugural professional season: two groups of 10, group winners Olympique Lillois and Cannes met in the final (Lille won 4-3). Third place as listed by the source (RC Paris); no third-place match was played. Points are not comparable across the two groups and are omitted

Official championship suspended due to the Second World War; unofficial wartime championships (regional/zone competitions, and the 1943-44 federal-team championship) were played but are not counted by the LFP. Unofficial wartime competition (not counted): 1939-40: regional groups; Rouen (North) and Girondins ASP (South) won their sections, the national final was never played (German invasion)

Unofficial wartime competition (not counted): 1943-44: Federal Championship of 16 regional teams (professional clubs dissolved by the Vichy government); won by Lens-Artois, partly unfinished

Official championship suspended due to the Second World War; unofficial wartime championships (regional/zone competitions, and the 1943-44 federal-team championship) were played but are not counted by the LFP. Unofficial wartime competition (not counted): 1944-45: post-Liberation league of 2 groups and a final, won by Rouen
Toulouse FC (1937) is a different club from today's Toulouse FC (founded 1970); it merged into Red Star in 1967
RC Paris-Sedan was the 1966-70 merger of Racing Club de Paris and UA Sedan-Torcy (today CS Sedan Ardennes)
